newsitem.title: NIGER: Meningitis kills 450 in Niger in 1997, cholera six.
newsitem.headline: Meningitis kills 450 in Niger in 1997, cholera six.

text.p: Meningitis killed 450 people in the Sub-Saharan West African state of Niger in the first six months of 1997 and cholera killed six people in the same period, health officials said.

The capital Niamey, with 58 deaths among 523 cases, was the worst hit by the outbreak of meningitis -- a disease which occurs every year across the Sahelian desert fringe of Africa during the dry season.
Cholera killed 206 people in 1996, Meningitis killed more than 700 people in the first quarter of 1996 alone. In 1995, meningitis killed more than 4,000 people.
